title: Cut or open wound
summary: Control bleeding, rinse superficial wounds, cover cleanly, and assess deep or contaminated wounds.
sources: 2024 American Heart Association and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid — Superficial Wounds
WHO Basic Emergency Care: Approach to the Acutely Ill and Injured
actions: For heavy bleeding, apply firm direct pressure and follow the severe-bleeding guidance.
For a superficial wound, rinse thoroughly with clean running water or saline until visible dirt is removed. Clean the surrounding skin.
Cover with a clean dressing. Change it if wet or dirty.

Seek prompt care for deep or gaping wounds, bites, embedded material, loss of feeling or movement, heavy contamination, or a wound over a joint, hand, face, or genitals. Tetanus protection may need review.
Watch for increasing redness, swelling, pain, drainage, or fever.
prohibitions: Do not pour harsh chemicals into the wound.
Do not remove a deeply embedded object.
Do not close a deep, dirty, or bite wound yourself.

emergencyCall.text: Call emergency services for life-threatening bleeding; deep, gaping, contaminated, numb, or function-limiting wounds need prompt care.
